HPI: 24 yo f with no chronic medical conditions presents to clinic c/o burning with urination that started 2 days ago and right flank pain that started yesterday. Symptoms are progressively worsening. Flank pain is located in the right flank below the ribs, radiates toward the right groin, is a dull constant ache rated 7/10 (worst 8/10). Dysuria is burning, 5/10, only with voiding. Worse with movement and jarring; partially relieved by ibuprofen and a heating pad. Associated with subjective fever, shaking chills last night, nausea with one episode of emesis this morning, urinary frequency and urgency, and cloudy malodorous urine. Denies gross hematuria. Had a bladder infection 6 months ago treated with antibiotics; never involved the back. Tried ibuprofen, cranberry juice and increased fluids without relief. Concerned this is damaging her kidneys because an aunt required dialysis.

PMH: No chronic medical conditions. UTI 6 months ago.
PSH: Wisdom tooth extraction age 18. No hospitalizations.
Meds: Oral contraceptive 1 tab daily; ibuprofen 400 mg a couple of times daily for the past 2 days.
SH: Graduate student, lives with my husband. Never smoker. 2-3 alcoholic drinks on weekends. No illicit drug use. Sexually active with one male partner, inconsistent condom use, no new partners. LMP 3 weeks ago, regular; pregnancy possible.
FH: Mother 52 with HTN. Father 55 with type 2 DM. One older brother, healthy. No kidney disease or stones in parents or brother; maternal aunt required dialysis, cause unknown.
Allergies: Sulfa - hives.
ROS: GU - admits dysuria, frequency, urgency; denies gross hematuria. GI - admits nausea and vomiting; denies diarrhea and constipation. General - admits subjective fever and chills; denies weight loss. Denies vaginal discharge, cough, chest pain, rash, headache.
model_note.O:
Vitals: T 101.6 F oral, P 104 bpm, BP 112/70 mmHg, R 18 rpm, Pulse Ox 99% on room air, Ht 5'5", Wt 138 lbs

General: Young woman appearing uncomfortable, shifting in the chair, in mild distress. Alert and oriented.
Heart: Tachycardic, regular rhythm, S1 and S2 present, no murmurs, rubs or gallops.
Lungs: CTA bilaterally anterior and posterior. Good air movement. No rales, rhonchi or wheezes.
Abd: Bowel sounds present and normoactive in 4 quadrants, no bruits. Tympanitic throughout. Soft, non-distended. Tenderness RUQ and right flank. No rebound, no guarding, no masses, no organomegaly. Murphy sign negative. McBurney point non-tender.
GU: Right CVA tenderness markedly positive; left CVA non-tender. Pelvic exam refused.
Skin: No rashes or lesions.
Labs: Point-of-care urine dipstick - leukocyte esterase positive, nitrites positive, trace blood, trace protein, glucose negative.
Osteopathic: T10-L1 right paraspinal tissue texture change, tenderness and hypertonicity; T11 rotated right.
P: 1. Obtain urine culture and urinalysis, pregnancy test, CBC and BMP; assess current stability, oral intake, obstruction and sepsis risk. Choose a renal-tissue-penetrating antibiotic through the clinician using allergy, pregnancy, local resistance and culture information; avoid the reported sulfonamide allergen. Do not use nitrofurantoin to treat pyelonephritis. Arrange emergency evaluation now if unstable, unable to retain fluids or at risk of infected obstruction; otherwise establish follow-up in 48–72 hours with culture review. Educate on the prescribed course, hydration and urgent deterioration precautions.

2. Assess for a ureteral stone with appropriate renal imaging when obstruction is suspected; provide clinician-directed analgesia and antiemetic and consult urology urgently for infected obstruction. Explain that fever with obstruction cannot be managed by hydration alone; defer manipulative treatment during acute systemic illness.

3. Obtain pregnancy testing and urgent pelvic ultrasound with Doppler if torsion remains clinically suspected; seek urgent gynecology evaluation based on suspicion rather than waiting for a reassuring Doppler result. Provide clinician-directed pain control and educate about sudden severe pelvic pain and emergency return.

Choose a renal-tissue-penetrating antibiotic through the clinician using allergy, pregnancy, local resistance and culture information; avoid the reported sulfonamide allergen. Do not use nitrofurantoin to treat pyelonephritis. Explain that fever with obstruction cannot be managed by hydration alone; defer manipulative treatment during acute systemic illness.
